summary: Daily sales team stand-up run by Chris Klevan with closer Ben Byrne and setter Kim Forbes-Sobers: wins, then setter projections (Kim at 18 of 20 sets, 75% show rate, challenged to add four more) and Ben's three calls on the calendar plus weekend slots. Kim describes the setter framework — current situation, biggest problem, why change now, goals and why they matter, then financials. After Kim leaves the call becomes a manager 1-1 between Chris and Ben on Ben's discovery-to-close gap: Chris coaches him to get a clear yes or no, never end on 'maybe', and to take the sale when it is offered rather than keep talking. They also cover the financing stack (PayPal Credit and Payvo primary, Klarna deprecated, Affirm lost) and role-play the 'is that all up front for the 6k' question.
notable: Stated financing stack: 'We do have Klarna, but it's just not, like, I would probably start with PayPal credit now' and 'for now, PayPal credit and pay vote' — Affirm was previously used and lost: 'We used to have Affirm, but something happened with an old closer and I guess they lost it.'

Ben describes routing around lender restrictions on coaching programmes: 'basically like Affirm and Klarna, don't really like coaching programs. So like the way to, there's like a way to do it where they got to go through like Apple pay.'

Stated payment-plan framing for the $6,000 offer, role-played by the manager: 'yeah most people just start on a credit card take care of it that way why do you ask' — i.e. deflect the up-front question rather than open a plan conversation.
Manager policy statement on call endings: 'Do not end calls on maybe' and 'When the guy's giving you the sale, just take it.'
Manager scripts a financial pre-qualification line to be used mid-call: 'are you in a position where you could invest thousands of dollars in yourself to make that change'.
Setter qualification framework stated by Kim: current situation, goals, biggest problem, why change now, why the goals matter, 'And then financials as well.'
Ben is new to the offer — Chris references 'probably been your seventh live call' — which is context for scoring his adherence in this date range.

Manager pressed the setter to raise output above her own stated projection ('Can I challenge you to get four more so that way we can get Ben some calls on Saturday and Sunday?') after she said she was not confident in the higher number.
